title: Fagiolini in Umido
subtitle: Green beans braised in tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil
excerpt: Green beans cooked slowly in a simple tomato sauce until tender and full of flavour. A classic Italian side that works alongside almost any main.
sourceNotes: Traditional Italian braised green bean preparation found throughout Tuscany and central Italy.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a larger batch and serve over two days. The flavour improves overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook a few hours ahead and reheat gently. Green beans hold well in the sauce.

content.text: Fagiolini in umido are braised, not blanched. The beans cook inside the tomato sauce and absorb it as they soften. Use a lid to trap the steam during the first half of cooking. Remove it later to let the sauce concentrate.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Do not let it brown.
Add the green beans and stir to coat. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Break them up with a spoon. Put the lid on and cook on a low heat for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid. Cook for a further 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the beans are very tender.
Stir through the basil. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve warm.

items.symptom: The beans are still tough after 30 minutes.
items.cause: The heat was too low or the beans were very thick.
items.fix: Add a splash of water, put the lid back on, and cook for another 10 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce is catching on the bottom.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough liquid.
items.fix: Add 50ml of water and stir, then reduce the heat to its lowest setting.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning or the basil was added too early and lost its flavour.
items.fix: Taste and add more salt. Stir in a second handful of fresh basil just before serving.
